policy: No pair is automatically equivalent. Names are candidates only; review identity, lifecycle, tenant scope, constraints, and data meaning before migration.

mappings.reason: Both represent activities, but SQLite uses person-oriented owner IDs and text identifiers while Supabase uses UUID user IDs and optional organization scope.
Supabase product schema includes name/description/unit_name; SQLite product identity and fields differ and may be extended by later migrations.
Both model offers, but their IDs, pricing, currency, scope, location, and effective-time contracts differ.
Sales lifecycle and identifiers differ; Supabase includes user/org, idempotency, currency and amount fields.
Payment ownership, amount, status and relationship contracts require a field-level mapping before copying.
The Supabase documents table may support multiple document types; invoice equivalence and lifecycle have not been proven.
SQLite models effective-dated positions by activity/scope/location; Supabase inventory is linked to offerings and has a different quantity model.
A financial account is not necessarily the same entity as a party account; do not merge without a domain-approved contract.
Ledger entries and journal entries are different accounting concepts and cannot be merged by matching names.
Both are audit-related, but payload, actor identity, target identity, retention and immutability rules differ.
